Managing Director --Petitioner
 Versus
Ram Kishan Arora & Others --Respondents
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Mr. Ashish Joshi, Advocate, for the
petitioner.
(2) Petitioner has challenged the
order dated 24.1.2026, passed by
Controlling Authority under sub-section (3-
A) of Section 7 of Payment of Gratuity Act,
1972. Petitioner has also challenged
subsequent order dated 11.3.2026, passed
on petitioner's correction application.
Perusal of the impugned order reveals that
respondent was terminated from service
w.e.f. 7.11.1997, and he had earlier
rendered more than 22 years of service on
the post of Conductor. Since gratuity was
paid to respondent only on 8.11.2019,
therefore, Controlling Authority directed
petitioner to pay interest @ 10 per cent per
annum for the delayed payment of gratuity
to respondent.
(3) This Court do not find any reason
to interfere with the orders impugned in the
writ petition. Sub-section (2), (3) and (3-A)
of Section 7 of Payment of Gratuity Act are
extracted below:
"(2) As soon as gratuity becomes payable,
the employer shall, whether an application referred to
in sub-section (1) has been made or not, determine
the amount of gratuity and give notice in writing to the
person to whom the gratuity is payable and also to the
controlling authority specifying the amount of gratuity
so determined.

UKHC010112392026
2026:UHC:5496
(3) The employer shall arrange to pay the
amount of gratuity within thirty days from the date it
becomes payable to the person to whom the gratuity
is payable.
(3-A) If the amount of gratuity payable
under sub-section (3) is not paid by the employer
within the period specified in sub-section (3), the
employer shall pay, from the date on which the
gratuity becomes payable to the date on which it is
paid, simple interest at such rate, not exceeding the
rate notified by the Central Government from time to
time for repayment of long-term deposits, as that
Government may, by notification specify:
Provided that no such interest shall be payable if
the delay in the payment is due to the fault of the
employee and the employer has obtained permission
in writing from the controlling authority for the delayed
payment on this ground."
(4) As per the scheme of the Act, the
amount payable as gratuity has to be
determined by employer, whether or not an
application has been made therefor by the
employee, and the amount so determined
has to be paid to the employee within 30
days from the date it becomes payable.
Since services of respondent were
terminated w.e.f. 7.11.1997, therefore, it
was incumbent upon the employer
(petitioner herein) to calculate the amount
payable as gratuity and to make payment
to the respondent within 30 days i.e. on or
before 6.12.1997. The amount of gratuity
was paid to the respondent only on
8.11.2019. Sub-section (3-A) of Section 7
unequivocally provides that the employee
shall be entitled to simple interest at such
rate, not exceeding the rate specified by
the Central Government, for the delayed
payment of amount of gratuity.
(5) Learned Counsel for the petitioner
concedes that Central Government issued
notification, wherein rate of interest
payable under sub-section (3-A) of Section

UKHC010112392026
2026:UHC:5496
7 of the Act is specified as 10 per cent.
Learned Counsel for the petitioner, however,
contends that respondent challenged the
order of termination passed against him in
the year 1997 by raising an industrial
dispute, which was referred for adjudication
to the Labour Court, and the Labour Court
decided the reference in favour of
respondent vide award dated 28.5.1999;
the award rendered by Labour Court was
challenged by the employer before this
Court in Writ Petition (M/S) No. 1209 of
2000, wherein an interim direction was
issued to petitioner to ensure compliance of
Section 17(B) of Industrial Disputes Act,
1947; in terms of the interim direction of
this Court, respondent was reinstated in
service w.e.f. 7.5.2000; said writ petition
was partly allowed vide judgment dated
5.8.2005, passed by coordinate Bench of
this Court, petitioner was directed to
reinstate the petitioner in service; however,
respondent was again disengaged on
30.5.2007, when Hon'ble Supreme Court
decided the SLP filed by the employer in his
favour and set aside the award rendered by
the Labour Court as well as the judgment
passed by coordinate Bench of this Court,
vide judgment dated 9.5.2007. Thus it is
contended that gratuity became payable to
respondent only on 9.5.2007, when SLP
filed by employer was decided against the
respondent and the award of Labour Court
as well as judgment rendered by coordinate
Bench of this Court were set aside.
(6) This Court is not impressed by the
said submission. Since termination of
service of respondent was effected on
7.11.1997, therefore, as per the scheme of
Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, gratuity

UKHC010112392026
2026:UHC:5496
became payable to him within 30 days from
the date of his termination i.e. on or before
6.12.1997. In the year 1997, when
respondent was terminated from service,
no one had contemplated that he would be
reinstated in terms of the award rendered
by Labour Court for certain period and
thereafter he would again be disengaged
from service in view of the judgment
rendered by Hon'ble Supreme Court. Thus
the contention raised on behalf of petitioner
that gratuity became payable to respondent
only on 9.5.2007, when Hon'ble Supreme
Court decided the SLP in favour of
employer, cannot be accepted. The
impugned orders are in conformity with the
provision contained in sub-section (3) and
(3-A) of Section 7 of Payment of Gratuity
Act, 1972.
(7) For the reasons aforesaid, there is
no scope of interference in the matter. Writ
petition fails and is dismissed.
 (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
